err.message: expected '{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"An…' to include 'later merge targets defer publication'
err.actual:
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Anthracite workflow for agents

Authority: follow higher-priority user and repository instructions. Connection,
discovery and this guide do not authorize staging, committing or publishing.
Honor the owner's existing approval process for PR titles, descriptions and
publication. Tool annotations are hints, not permission.

A stack is a chain of tracked branches based on a trunk (usually main).
Downstack means toward trunk; upstack means toward descendant branches.
Inspect first with an log, an info and ordinary git status/diff. Every
run_an_cmd request must supply an explicit absolute cwd for the intended project,
an argument array (not a shell command) and a why explanation. For example:
{"args": ["log"], "cwd": "/absolute/project", "why": "Inspect the stack"}

Use the user's normal tooling to stage only intended changes (for example,
git add path/to/file). With staged work, an create feature -m "Describe change"
creates a branch and commit. On an existing branch, an modify -m "Describe change"
updates its commit and restacks affected descendants; an restack replays a stack
onto its recorded parents. There is no universal requirement to create a branch
before editing: follow the repository's workflow and inspect current state.
Use an <command> --help for supported selectors and options; supply required
choices explicitly because MCP execution is non-interactive.

Use an get [branch] (alias g) for authorized feature-head refresh. A branch or
numeric PR argument selects the target; omission uses the original physical
current branch. Detached HEAD requires an explicit target. Trunk itself remains
a no-op, not an all-stacks selector. By default, get refreshes the required PR
ancestor chain and eligible tracked local descendants of the target, then
restacks affected local work and selects the target on complete success.
--downstack limits remote refresh to the required chain; necessary local sibling
maintenance can still fall outside that refresh selection. Independent trunk
stacks remain outside get, and remote-only descendants are not discovered.
For explicit old-selection/no-replay behavior, use an get target --downstack
--no-restack. This still permits safe trunk fast-forward and is not a promise of
identical old execution. --no-checkout independently restores the original
physical branch identity at its current authorized head, or the exact detached
OID, only after all enabled phases finish. Intermediate checkouts can occur.
For example, a literal MCP request is:
{"args": ["get", "target", "--downstack", "--no-restack", "--no-checkout"], "cwd": "/absolute/project", "why": "Refresh the authorized chain and retain checkout"}
Trunk advances by fast-forward only; feature --force never resets trunk. Feature
force is bounded to eligible selected incoming sources and preserves frozen
status plus local-file/worktree protections. Local-only descendants retain their
own work; missing required sources and service failures are errors, not skips.
New imports use per-PR ownership verification: verified own imports are editable,
other or unknown authors are frozen, and --unfrozen/-U overrides new imports only.
Automatic maintenance retains frozen anchors and names skipped or deferred work.
Get performs no cleanup, pushes or PR writes; sync retains its separate defaults.
A saved get conflict returns cli_error with reached updates and actual checkout.
Resolve deliberately in the printed original worktree, stage intended resolutions
and call an continue (or cont). The owned operation retains pinned sources,
parents, import decisions and saved get replay/checkout policy across processes;
remaining protections are checked before --all stages or advances. Raw Git abort
cancels only its active rebase, not earlier updates. Missing, foreign, changed or
aborted intent and ambiguous metadata/final-checkout failures require inspection;
never clear records or reset/recreate refs to pretend restoration succeeded.
Finish a pending graph-aware get before downgrading to an older release.

Use an sync (also repo sync or repo s) for repository-wide refresh of existing
tracked open-PR feature heads belonging to the single configured trunk, followed
by separately authorized local cleanup and default maintenance. Independent local
stacks are included; missing parents and remote-only branches are not imported.
For example, literal args ["sync", "--no-pull", "--no-delete"] refresh features
and repair affected histories while retaining trunk and cleanup candidates.
--no-pull controls trunk fetching/application only: PR reads and feature refresh
still occur. --no-delete suppresses cleanup even with --delete-all or --force.
--delete-all confirms only already eligible local cleanup. Sync --force retains
separate cleanup consent and trunk-reset authority; neither flag silently grants
feature overwrite. Local-ahead/divergent trunk now refuses without explicit force
or affirmative terminal reset consent, deliberately replacing the old local-ahead
no-op. Get keeps its independent FF-only trunk and target-bounded, cleanup-free
contract. --no-restack defers automatic replay, but not incoming updates, approved
cleanup/parent changes or a separately chosen terminal reconciliation rebase.
There is no exact old PR-information-only flag recipe or feature-refresh switch.
Booleans accept true/false and negative forms on all three routes; -p/-d/-f/-r
and --show-delete-progress remain supported.

Local-only work stays unpublished; closed/merged branches skip incoming refresh
and remain if cleanup is declined or protected. Disabled GitHub integration makes
no service calls and retains local sync without treating cached PR status as fresh.
Frozen inbound updates preserve status. Frozen histories skip local replay;
mandatory frozen survivors can exclude cleanup even with --no-restack. Eligible
survivors keep their PR identities and own commits/authors/full messages through
parent-first incoming updates, approved cleanup and affected local maintenance.
Full success restores the original surviving physical branch at its authorized
head or exact detached OID. Only actual approved deletion of that branch permits
the reported trunk fallback. File collisions, tracked dirt and affected worktrees
remain protected; late failures retain reached work and concurrent actor state.

A real owned sync conflict returns cli_error. Resolve deliberately in the printed
original project and use an continue/cont in a fresh call. The saved sync intent
retains pinned sources, graph, consent, remaining phases and checkout policy;
protections are rechecked before --all stages or advances. PR-based pending cleanup
requires fresh reads of the exact saved identities/states and may need GitHub read
access; disabled integration, changed PRs or failed lookup refuse advancement.
No new candidates or source heads are discovered on resume. Raw Git abort cancels
only the active rebase, not earlier updates, cleanup or completed rewrites. Missing,
foreign, changed, aborted or no-active intent and uncertain completed publication
require manual inspection, not automatic retry or rollback. To end a supported
owned sync, run an sync --abort in the original project. This is local and offline:
it archives the original intent and source observations, quits only its matching
active rebase, and releases only the sync gate. Repeating after completion is a
no-op. Reached updates, source pins, conflicts, index and files stay preserved;
no rollback, staging, checkout, branch deletion, push or PR edit is performed.
An owned autostash is retained without applying/discarding it. Handle residual
Git/files deliberately before guarded deletion or a new sync. Unknown PR status
is not evidence that a branch has no PR. Do not combine --abort with explicit
refresh/cleanup/force/restack options. Malformed/foreign ownership still refuses.
Full/short log and ls inspect supported pending sync without consuming recovery.
Attached HEAD is current; detached pending intent anchors selection only and is
not a checked-out branch. Explicit zero depth still refuses detached HEAD.
Some source refs may already have been removed. Finish a pending new sync
workflow before downgrading.
Sync never pushes or edits PRs. Existing MCP tools, literal cwd/args, supervision
and publication approvals remain unchanged; cancellation does not promise undo.

To insert a prerequisite below selected direct children, use an create shared
--insert --onto parent --insert-child left --insert-child right -m "Prerequisite".
The c alias and -i also work. Each --insert-child consumes one exact literal
branch name, including commas or numeric-looking names, and requires active
--insert. Children belong to --onto, otherwise the current branch or trunk.
Explicit choices suppress the child menu; without them MCP and other
noninteractive calls still move all children. In a terminal, multiple children
open a menu with all initially selected and at least one required. Selection
precedes staging and creation. Only chosen children and necessary descendants
are mandatory for frozen/worktree checks; independent unselected arms stay put.
A real replay conflict returns failure with retained work: resolve deliberately
and use an continue in a fresh call. Saved selected scope is retained and pending
mandatory participants are rechecked before --all stages or advances. Raw Git
abort does not roll back inserted commits, parent changes or completed replays.
Insertion does not push or change PRs; existing publication approval still applies.

For review corrections, an absorb (alias ab) assigns staged ordinary text hunks
to their exact original commits in the current downstack and replays mandatory
descendants. Preview with an absorb --dry-run (ab -d), then explicitly apply with
an absorb --force (ab -f): MCP has no terminal confirmation. --all/-a includes
tracked updates/deletions and existing staged entries, never untracked files;
--patch/-p requires a real terminal and cannot run through MCP. Unsupported entry
changes and unmatched hunks remain staged and are reported. Absorb does not fetch,
push or change PRs. Frozen targets are excluded; a frozen or occupied mandatory
participant refuses before staging or rewriting, even with --force.
After an owned absorb replay conflict, resolve and stage only the resolution,
then use an continue in the original worktree. Retained staged/unstaged input is
kept separately until checked restoration. Ref/protection/worktree and Git
environment checks also apply on continue before --all. Other failures report
reached work and an executable guarded manual restoration path. Earlier amendments
survive raw Git abort; do not promise rollback or retry a noncontinuable failure.

Frozen branches and branches occupied in another worktree retain their existing
protections. Inspect the refusal and choose an allowed operation; do not bypass
these guards. After a conflict, inspect git status and the reported partial
state, resolve files deliberately and stage resolutions with normal tooling,
then use an continue. A disconnected or interrupted operation may need this
inspection after reconnecting; interruption does not promise rollback.
Cancellation and timeout stop owned work without rollback. Cancelling queued
work prevents it from starting; disconnect discards the queue. Interruption does
not erase Git recovery data or authorize an automatic retry. Inspect actual refs,
staged changes and continuation before proceeding.

Inspect GitHub with an pr [branch] (optional --stack includes connected fanout)
and an review [branch] for the actual base-to-head diff. Neither authorizes a
write. An explicit review action --approve, --request-changes or --comment must
include --head <full-oid> matching the fresh selected PR. Comment and changes
request need --body or --body-file; approval may omit it. Review submission is
separate from reviewer assignment. Uncertain review responses require inspection;
never automatically repeat a review POST or claim a newer head was approved.

Preview an land [branch] --dry-run. The merge set is the unique trunk-to-target
chain; necessary surviving descendants and sibling arms are maintenance only.
Only user-authorized application with --yes can merge that chain, replay local
survivors, push their existing heads, update existing PR bases/managed footers and
clean confirmed landed refs. Missing survivor PRs stay missing and unpublished
heads stay unpublished. Independent stacks stay outside scope. Every next merge
requires fresh expected-head readiness after maintenance. During confirmed
application or resumption, known running required checks are polled every five seconds
for up to 600 seconds per PR (--wait-timeout changes seconds; 0 stops immediately).
Dry-runs and initial preflight never wait. Optional running or failed checks are
reported without waiting or blocking. UNSTABLE alone does not block when verified
merge requirements pass. Failed required checks, dismissed approvals,
changed identities, unknown readiness, unreadable policy or missing publisher
provenance stop progress. Client deadlines may interrupt a wait sooner; inspect
preserved progress and explicitly resume rather than assuming rollback.
There is no queue, bypass, automatic approval or implicit submit route.

A landing conflict returns cli_error and retains completed merges and parents.
Resolve and stage deliberately, then an continue in the printed original project
performs local-only replay. It never merges, pushes or edits PRs. The landing
record remains until explicit an land [original-target] --yes revalidates and
finishes remote maintenance, even if that target branch was already deleted.
A durably completed preceding replay can retain an exact pending local queue;
freeze/worktree/ref guards still apply. Public unfreeze changes protection only.
Raw Git abort cancels only the active rebase. Ambiguous replay or metadata
publication requires guarded manual inspection; never clear recovery or assume
rollback. Exact owned dead-process locks can be reconciled by explicit resumption;
foreign, live, invalid or unproven locks remain. Inspect after cancellation or
reconnect before authorizing another call. Same-repository github.com only;
adapter acceptance does not establish live-service or enterprise compatibility.

Submit deliberately with an submit (or an submit --help to inspect selectors).
Reviewer and assignee lists apply to every selected PR by default. Use
--roles-branch <exact-local-branch> to add both lists only to that selected PR;
this does not narrow the submission scope selected by --branch or --stack. Preview
with --dry-run, then supply --reviewers and --assignees explicitly. Assignees accept
@me for the authenticated GitHub user. Existing roles are retained; role options
do not publish drafts. After a failure, inspect confirmed and unattempted work
before repeating the command.
Confirm intended branches, PR metadata and the owner's publication approval
before pushing or changing PRs. Anthracite reuses GitHub CLI credentials; it
requires no Graphite token or additional MCP account. Missing authentication is
handled by the normal CLI; learning and discovery do not log in or initialize a
repository automatically.
"}]}
